description: We’re cupcakkemas gang, a team of four uni students building SPHEREx Blink for the “Planet X and SPHEREx” challenge: a web tool where you enter a sky position and watch a time-lapse of real SPHEREx images, so moving objects like comets, asteroids and brown dwarfs stand out. Our skills: Python data pipelines, image processing, web frontend and documentation. Our team is full for this event, but we’re happy to share what we learn.
summary: We developed a public web tools that help users discover moving object objects in the sky using real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations. Users enter a sky position in Right Ascension and Declination, and the tool retrieves time-ordered image cutouts from NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). These images are aligned and presented as an animation so objects that move can be identified easily. The tool supports known targets including Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae and R Draconis. This addresses the challenge by transforming SPHEREx's vast and complex dataset into an accessible discovery interface fro public. It is important because it lowers the barrier to astronomical research and enables people explore a continuously expanding infrared map of the universe.
details:
SPHEREx Blink allows user to enter sky position using Right Ascension(RA) and Declination(Dec) coordinates in either decimal or sexagesimal format. It then display real SPHEREx images of the selected sky region in a time-ordered animation, allowing user to observe changes and identify moving objects over time.

The tool tranform a specialist astronomical archive into a simple visual search experience. Instead of downloading large astronomical files or learning complex archive query language, user can enter coordinates and inspect images for moving or changing objects. The intended impact is to make the search for nearby stars, brown dwarfs, comets, asteroids and other changing objects more accesible to students, the public and citizen scientists.

The project use Python 3.10+, FastAPI and Uvicorn for the web API and server, with HTML, CSS and JavaScript for frontend interface. It also integrates Astropy for astronomical coordinate handling, FITS file processing and World Coordinate System (WCS), alongside Reproject for image alignment and Numpy and Pillow for image processing and PNG generation. Real SPHEREx observational data are obtained through NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), while Gaia and SIMBAD are used as astronomical references sources for target verification.

In addition to the blinking animation, SPHEREx Blink provides three viewing modes: All Frames, Stack by Detector and Difference Imaging. The features allow users to compare observation chronologically, combine images from individual detectors to improve the visibility of faint sources and highlight changes by subtracting a reference image. The tool also provides observation metadata and a spectrum API to retrieve information such as flux, error, wavelength, observation date and detector values for a selected pixel.

The project focus on providing reliable results using real astronomical observations while considering challenges such as image alignment, changing wavelength, object proper motion, archive availability and response time. Overall SPHEREx Blink aims to simplify the exploration of infrared astronomical data and encourage greater public participation in discovering interesting and potentially moving object in the universe.
